SMTO-EXE-0123 — SMTO's browser can't do that on this page

GUID: 8c63517d-1394-5929-9d74-e2f69591bd46
Slug: browser-unsupported-operation
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO's browser couldn't carry out this step, often because the tab shows something other than a normal web page. SMTO hadn't started the action, so the page wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO: "Which page is your browser showing now?" SMTO's browser only works with pages whose address starts with http:// or https://.
  2. If it shows a browser settings page, a local file, a PDF viewer or a blank error page, ask SMTO to go to the normal web address you need. Special pages like these can be viewed but not read or clicked by SMTO.
  3. If SMTO was connecting to your own open browser, make sure that browser is running with a normal window open, then ask SMTO to connect again. SMTO needs an open browser window to connect to.
  4. Ask SMTO to check its browser status on this Gateway and tell you what it reports. The status shows whether the browser on the Gateway is working at all.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the step on a normal web page and reports the result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the web address and what you asked SMTO to do, to the person who manages the Gateway. The details won't include the browser's internal error text, so describe the page too.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway browser service rejected or failed an operation before any effect: the page is not an http(s) page, the attached browser exposed no context, the action is unsupported, or an unclassified pre-action error occurred.

What this means

  • The backend lacks a supported attached context, rejects page semantics outside supported URLs/main-frame operations, or catches an unclassified pre-effect failure. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • The backend lacks a supported attached context, rejects page semantics outside supported URLs/main-frame operations, or catches an unclassified pre-effect failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect browser.status, session kind, page URL and the operation boundary; do not infer an unsupported site feature from every backend exception.

How to fix it

  • Raised by PlaywrightBackend.execute for non-http(s) pages (other than navigate/close_tab/page_info) or an unknown action, by _start when an attached CDP browser has no contexts, by BrowserError for unknown kinds, and by BrowserService._execute for an unclassified exception before mark(). Inspect browser.status and browser.page_info; navigate to an http(s) URL; only Chromium main-frame operations are supported and provider diagnostics are not exposed.
  • Inspect browser.status and the current page. This backend supports Chromium and main-frame semantics only; provider diagnostics are not exposed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect browser.status and the current page. This backend supports Chromium and main-frame semantics only; provider diagnostics are not exposed.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported operation produces a valid result, or the unsupported requirement remains explicitly unmet.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
